messages.content:
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment
Definition: AI systems must not be used for making clinical decisions, determining diagnoses, or treatment plans. Clinicians remain personally accountable for all decisions regarding patient care, and AI outputs require validation before use.
Policy Type: C

Candidate risks:
- 1: Inadequate observability (Slatteryet al., 2024) — The AI system may lack sufficient logging or traceability features, making it difficult to monitor or audit its decision-making process after the fact.
  Cross-mappings: ail-suicide-and-self-harm[related], atlas-unreliable-source-attribution[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.3[related]
- 2: Lack of transparency or interpretability — Challenges in understanding or explaining the decision-making processes of AI systems, which can lead to mistrust, difficulty in enforcing compliance standards or holding relevant actors accountable for harms, and the inability to identify and correct errors.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-005[related], credo-risk-006[related], credo-risk-007[related]
- 3: Regulatory compliance — The AI system may fail to comply with existing or emerging regulations and standards, potentially leading to legal penalties,fines, or operational restrictions.
  Cross-mappings: granite-guardian-harm[related], atlas-legal-accountability[related], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-6.4[related]
- 4: Over or under-reliance and unsafe use (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023) — Users may inappropriately rely on the AI system for critical decisions or tasks beyond its capabilities, or fail to put trust in AI systems when they should, potentially leading to errors or safety issues.
  Cross-mappings: atlas-over-or-under-reliance[close], mit-ai-risk-subdomain-5.1[close], granite-guardian-harm[related]
- 5: Lack of robustness (Slattery et al., 2024) — The AI system's performance may fail to generalize well to new environments or inputs, potentially leading to unexpected failures or degraded performance in real-world applications.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-7.3[close], llm082025-vector-and-embedding-weaknesses[related]

matched_risks.justification: Directly addresses the risk of clinicians relying on AI for clinical decisions without proper validation.
Relates to the need for understanding AI outputs before using them in clinical decisions.
Concerns the ability to audit AI decision-making, which is important for validating clinical use.
